To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Arabidopsis plants can use DNA as a phosphorus source; 2) a screen for conditional mutations in Arabidopsis that affect DNA utilization has been developed; 3) a number of mutants that are defective in the utilization of DNA as a phosphorous source have been isolated and characterized; and 4) these mutants may affect regulatory components of the phosphate-starvation-response pathway.
we have identified a novel genetic pathway that controls expression of genes required for plant growth under phosphate-limiting growth conditions.
we have devised a screen to identify mutants defective in phosphate-starvation response, and we have isolated a mutant that is defective in the expression of phosphate-starvation response genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of mutants that are impaired in their ability to sense and adapt to low phosphate availability.
the identification and characterization of genes that are involved in the signal transduction of phosphate availability and in the regulation of phosphate-starvation-induced genes in higher plants.

the identification and characterization of mutants in Arabidosis thaliana (Arabidosis) that are defective in their ability to sense phosphate limitation and respond accordingly by inducing phosphate-starvation-induction genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the psr mutants are defective in a pathway that is required for sensing and responding to phosphate deficiency in Arabidopsis.

we identified a new mutant in the Arabidopsis thialiana that is defective in a signal transduction pathway that senses and transmits the phosphate-starvation signal to the phosphate-starvation-response pathway.
the psr1 mutation affects a component of the phosphate starvation response pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified mutants that are defective in the utilization of DNA as a phosphate source and that we have identified a mutant defective in the expression of a phosphate starvation response.
we identified a novel signaling pathway in plants that is involved in the regulation of phosphate starvation response.
we have identified a novel signaling pathway that is involved in the sensing and integration of the phosphate-starvation-response in Arabidopsis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Arabidopsis plants have a conditional ability to utilize DNA and RNA as sources of phosphorus and that a subset of conditional mutants in the utilization of these nucleic acids may be useful in dissecting the signaling pathways that sense low phosphate availability in plants.
we have devised a screen to identify genes involved in the phosphate-starvation-response in plants.
the conditional identification of mutants in the Pi starvation response is a powerful tool for the dissection of signal transduction pathways in higher plants.
